description: Default capability set for the main wallet window.
_comment: Every plugin grant here is the specific command the wallet calls, not the
plugin's `default` set. The defaults are wider than the wallet's use:
`updater:default` is four commands (check, download, install,
download_and_install) where the wallet calls two; `process:default` adds
`exit` which nothing calls; `opener:default` adds `reveal_item_in_dir`,
which has no caller anywhere in the frontend.
opener is NARROWED, NOT DROPPED. The plugin injects a click interceptor
into the webview that rewrites `target=_blank` anchors into a
`plugin:opener|open_url` IPC call, so every outbound link in the app
depends on it even though no module imports the plugin. allow-default-urls
is the SCOPE half (mailto/tel/http/https); without it open_url is granted
but every URL is refused.
The store plugin is GONE, not narrowed. Its `load` command took the file
path from the caller and resolved it with a bare push onto the app-data
directory, so an absolute, UNC or drive-relative path discarded the base
and `..` survived — reaching a read and a write. The plugin ships no scope
mechanism, so no permission here could have constrained it. Persistence now
goes through `wallet_store_read`/`wallet_store_write`, which take a store
IDENTIFIER from a closed set and resolve the path in Rust.
Wallet-owned commands are NOT listed here. `tauri::generate_handler!`
commands are reachable without a capability entry; this file governs PLUGIN
commands only. That is why removing a grant is what closes a plugin route.
The updater plugin's commands are gone for the same reason. Its `check`
accepted `proxy`, `headers`, `target` and `allowDowngrades` from the caller,
and `proxy` redirects BOTH the manifest fetch and the bundle download to a
host of the caller's choosing, bypassing the CSP connect-src allowlist. It
could not be narrowed away, because `check` is the command that carries it
and `check` is the command the wallet needs. `wallet_update_check` and
`wallet_update_install` call UpdaterBuilder in Rust with no caller
parameters at all.
The updater plugin stays REGISTERED in lib.rs even so: `updater_builder()`
reads state that the plugin's own Builder manages, so unregistering it
would panic those commands. Removing the capability is what makes its IPC
commands unreachable from the webview.
